extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, mathematics educators, and academic administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Arguments and standards for preserving graduate mathematics programs and for high-quality undergraduate instruction and mathematical communication in the media. Also includes evaluative guidance for reporters and authors on presenting mathematics to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research-active faculty for advanced graduate instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: To teach these [advanced mathematical subjects] with sophistication and insight requires people for whom they are the primary research interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graduate-level and advanced interdisciplinary subjects (e.g., theoretical geophysics, physical oceanography, digital imaging) should be taught by faculty who are active researchers in those areas; hiring nonresearch or out-of-field instructors is unlikely to provide the necessary sophistication or depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain graduate mathematics to support sciences and engineering
rubrics_metrics.description: If graduate mathematics is eliminated, I really don't see how [the university] can support first-rate programs in the sciences and in engineering, and I fear that all of these will decline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A university's ability to sustain strong science and engineering programs depends on a robust mathematics graduate program; eliminating the latter can degrade research and teaching quality across related disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not base major administrative decisions solely on rankings
rubrics_metrics.description: I simply do not think that these NRC 'ratings' are serious enough to be used for administrative decisions at universities.... I do not think that the U. S. News & World Report has any standing whatever as a serious source of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specialized departmental strengths and subfield excellence can be masked by broad ranking metrics. Administrators should not rely primarily on U.S. News, NRC rankings, or similar lists when deciding program elimination or restructuring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value specialized departmental strengths
rubrics_metrics.description: The Rochester Mathematics Department has chosen to specialize in analysis and in homotopy theory... This choice seems to me reasonable for a smaller university. However, it may have a strong effect on ratings...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that smaller departments may purposefully specialize in particular subfields; evaluation criteria should account for such specializations rather than penalizing them in aggregate rankings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Undergraduate instruction should be led by active mathematicians
rubrics_metrics.description: To attract and retain the brightest undergraduates requires that those who are responsible for instruction be active mathematicians and be aware of the ways that both the subject and its instruction are changing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teaching core undergraduate math (especially in the context of curriculum reform) requires instructors who are current in the discipline; delegating such instruction to non-mathematicians risks disconnect from pedagogical and content developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid relying primarily on adjuncts for core mathematics teaching
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a disservice to students and to the profession to relegate the teaching of mathematics to adjuncts and faculty from other disciplines.... such instruction is typically cheap, and you get what you pay for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjunct/temporary instruction often lacks the institutional support, commitment, and continuity needed for high-quality mathematics education; use of adjuncts for essential service courses is an anti-pattern likely to lower instructional quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional commitment to teaching quality
rubrics_metrics.description: High-quality teaching takes place only where it is a widely shared priority and people are respected for it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sustaining excellent teaching requires faculty morale, recognition, and an institutional culture that values pedagogy; restructuring that demoralizes research faculty can harm teaching quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service courses require knowledge of pedagogical reforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Keeping abreast of such change—in particular, major pedagogical and content changes in calculus—requires being connected to the mathematical community. Creating and delivering instruction consonant with reform requires both knowledge and commitment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementing modern calculus and related reforms demands instructors who understand current pedagogy; transferring these courses to outsiders without such knowledge is unlikely to produce desired instructional outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use concrete, dated examples when critiquing media math
rubrics_metrics.description: Almost never is a single newspaper article referenced, no newspaper article is discussed in any detail or quoted from, and even when a paper is mentioned, Paulos almost never gives the date of an article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When criticizing press coverage or demonstrating misuse of mathematics in media, authors should cite specific articles (with dates) and analyze them in detail; vague or undated references weaken the critique and reduce usefulness for readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make mathematics comprehensible to the general public
rubrics_metrics.description: For nonmathematicians, Paulos frequently is understandable, but at times he jumps too quickly into technicalities... Paulos does not seem to have taken care to make his mathematics comprehensible to the general public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Popular mathematics writing should avoid unnecessary jargon and provide clear explanations, stepping readers through technical ideas gently; dense, jargon-laden prose alienates the audience and reduces educational value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equip readers with analytic tools rather than only skepticism
rubrics_metrics.description: What may happen is that readers will become more skeptical of newspaper articles, especially those that go against their own prejudices or preconceptions, without having the tools to analyze the articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective popularizations should give readers concrete tools and heuristics to evaluate mathematical claims in the media; simply promoting skepticism without teaching how to analyze claims is counterproductive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporters should rely on experts, not attempt independent technical refereeing
rubrics_metrics.description: The job of a reporter is to discern in interviews whether experts in a field think that a finding is solid. We are not referees, and there is no way on earth that we or readers ... are going to be able to judge a result independently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists should consult and report expert consensus and disagreements rather than trying to perform independent technical validation; mathematicians should aid by explaining whether results are solid or overstated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify whether conclusions come from valid studies or anecdotes
rubrics_metrics.description: I wish more reporters would ask... whether conclusions were drawn from a valid study or a collection of anecdotes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A key journalistic check is to distinguish rigorous studies from anecdotal evidence; authors and reporters should explicitly signal the basis of claims and caution readers when evidence is anecdotal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess system dynamics when reporting on dynamical claims
rubrics_metrics.description: What is known about the dynamics of the whole system? Are they stable or do they seem sensitive to tiny perturbations?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a story involves dynamical systems (economics, climate, epidemiology, etc.), reporters should ask about stability and sensitivity to initial conditions; however, journalists should use experts to interpret technical answers rather than attempting deep technical judgments themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematicians should contextualize results for media
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematicians' jobs are to tell us if a result is less than it might seem or if it is better than we might realize.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When engaging with journalists, mathematicians should focus on clarifying the significance, limitations, and robustness of results to prevent misrepresentation and to help the public understand the true import of findings.
